description:
CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became. LS-DATE='1582-10-15' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='YYYY-MM-DD' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85); LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. This program opens no file and is reached by no JCL, so it seeds no dataset, writes no record and takes no job parameter - its entire observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at L42-L57 and the group move at L122, never captured from a COBOL run, which is impossible here - this program is itself one of the verified blockers, because PROCEDURE DIVISION USING (L88) cannot be linked as an executable and no Language Environment here supplies CEEDAYS (L116). Arm 1 of the EVALUATE TRUE at L128-L149: FC-INVALID-DATE, whose 88-level VALUE is X'0000000000000000' (L62) and which - despite its name - is the SUCCESS token. That inversion is preserved rather than repaired. Severity and message number are DECODED from that token rather than assumed: its first two halfwords are SEVERITY and MSG-NO (L72-L73), both of which read zero, which is why offset 0 carries 0000, offset 15 carries 0000 and RETURN-CODE is 0. This case pins arm 1 at the LOWER BOUNDARY of the supported range. 15 October 1582 is the Lillian epoch - day one of the count CEEDAYS returns in OUTPUT-LILLIAN (L41, L119) - so it converts, while case10 one day earlier does not; the year is a literal taken from that boundary and never from the clock. Pinning both sides of the boundary is what stops an off-by-one there passing as a range check that merely looks right. The TstDate: span also shows the L122 corruption plainly: the halfword 000A that L105-L106 set from LENGTH OF LS-DATE survives as the two leading bytes and only the first eight characters follow it, so the span reports 1582-10- and the 15 that separates this case from case10 is discarded - both cases carry an identical date span and are told apart only by severity, message number and result text. The mask at offset 66 is untouched by that move and stays clean.

THE TWO CALL PARAMETERS, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. unitStimulus.linkage carries this case's whole input: LS-DATE = '1582-10-15' and LS-DATE-FORMAT = 'YYYY-MM-DD', each written out to the ten characters PIC X(10) declares at app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:84-85 with every trailing space visible - a mask longer than ten characters is TRUNCATED by the receiving field, and the truncation changes the message number, so the width has to be readable at the point the value is written. CSUTLDTC seeds no dataset and drives no screen, so these two values are the only thing a case varies; they used to live in a table in CSUTLDTCParityTest keyed by 'case01'..'case20', which meant this file stated an eighty-byte result with nothing in it to say what was validated, and cases that differ only in their input were indistinguishable on disk.
